+== What asks first
+Camel TUI is a developer tool: the model works on your own machine, with your own integrations, and runs the
+TUI's tools without asking, so it can show and tell at once (see
+xref:security-model.adoc#_developer_tools[Developer tools] in the security model). It reads any tab, selects
+integrations and routes, starts and stops routes and infrastructure, sends test messages to the integration's
+endpoints and evaluates expressions. The few calls that reach beyond the integration, may destroy data or run
+code ask you first, in a dialog that shows the call:
+* writing a file: the diff dialog, or the live replay in the Source editor (see `/write` above);
+* sending a message to an endpoint the integration does not have, such as a file, a command, an HTTP service or
+  another topic; a message to a route, to an internal endpoint (`direct:`, `seda:`, `log:`, `mock:`, `stub:`
+  and the like), or to an endpoint the integration uses goes ahead;
+* SQL other than a single `SELECT`, `SHOW` or `DESCRIBE`, and updating a row;
+* evaluating an expression in a language that runs code, such as Groovy, Java, JavaScript or Python.
+*Enter* runs the call and *Esc* rejects it; the model is told that you rejected it. An HTTP request
+(`tui_http_request`) reaches only the integration's own server on `localhost`. While a tape records, or
+`--record` plays one, nothing asks. The same applies to a coding agent driving the panel and to an MCP client
+(see xref:camel-jbang-tui-ai-agents.adoc[AI agents]).

+=== Developer tools
+Camel CLI (`camel`) and Camel TUI (`camel tui`) are developer tools. They run
+on the developer's own machine, for the developer's own integrations, in the
+inner loop of writing and trying routes; they are not part of a production
+deployment. The developer is fully trusted, as a route author and an operator
+are, and so is the local machine: its user account, its loopback interface and
+the processes the developer starts.
+Camel TUI has AI assistants: the model of the AI panel (a local or a hosted
+LLM), a coding agent driving the panel over ACP, and an MCP client connected
+to `camel tui --mcp`. They act for the developer, and the TUI's tools let them
+do what the developer does in the TUI: read the screens, start and stop routes
+and infrastructure, send test messages to the integration, query its
+database, evaluate expressions and edit the project's files. To keep the
+feedback loop fast these tools run without asking. The guardrails are
+deliberately few, and they are the contract:
+* The file tools write only inside the integration's source directory, and
+  each write goes through the AI panel's write mode: a confirmation dialog
+  with the diff, or a replay in the source editor that the developer saves,
+  unless the developer chose `/write auto`.
+* The developer confirms a call that reaches beyond the integration, may
+  destroy data or runs code: a message to an endpoint the integration does not
+  have (a route, an internal endpoint such as `direct:`, `seda:` or `log:`,
+  and the integration's own endpoints are inside it), a SQL statement other
+  than a single `SELECT`, `SHOW` or `DESCRIBE`, a row update, and an
+  expression in a language that runs code, such as Groovy. An HTTP request
+  goes only to the integration's own server on `localhost`.
+* A coding agent's own tools - its shell commands, its file changes, its
+  network fetches - are put in front of the developer in the TUI.
+* Keys sent over MCP never answer a dialog that asks the developer to confirm
+  something.
+* While the developer records a tape, or plays one with `--record`, nothing
+  asks: the developer chose to let the model, the agent or the tape act alone.
+A tool that breaks this contract is in scope: for example a file written
+outside the source directory, a message sent to an endpoint the integration
+does not have without the developer's confirmation, or a key sent over MCP
+that answers a confirmation. An assistant doing what the tools allow is the
+trusted developer's case, also when untrusted data shown in the TUI - a
+message body, a log line, an example's README - steered the model to it
+(prompt injection); see _Out of scope_.
